sentences.text: TO ENLARGE THE PETITIONER ON BAIL IN CR.NO.83/2022 OF NYAMATHI P.S., DAVANAGERE DISTRICT

FOR THE OFFENCE P/U/S 506, 376(2)(n) OF IPC AND SEC.6 OF POCSO ACT ON THE FILE OF THE ADDL. DISTRICT AND SESSIONS JUDGE,
FTSC-1, DAVANAGERE IN S.C.NO.127/2022.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER Charge sheet has been filed against the petitioner for offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n)
and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred to as 'IPC' for short) and under Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter referred to as 'POCSO'
for short).
2.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Perusal of the charge sheet material would reveal that the accused with a promise of marriage and also stating that he is in love with the minor victim, subjected her to aggravated penetrative sexual assault.
Consequent to which, she became pregnant.
3. According to the prosecution, the date of birth of the victim is 27.06.2005 and therefore she was a minor, aged about 17 years as on the date of incident.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner would contend that the petitioner is innocent and a false case has been registered against him.
He contends that even earlier, the victim's mother had made similar allegations and a false case was registered against the petitioner, his brother and his mother which ultimately ended in acquittal.

5. In the statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., the victim has alleged that the petitioner has committed penetrative sexual assault on her by force and later she became pregnant and then there was a miscarriage.
6. Considering the above statement of the victim and since her evidence is not yet recorded, at this stage, if the petitioner is enlarged on bail, there is a chance of threatening or influencing her.

Hence,
this is not a fit case to enlarge the petitioner on bail at this stage.
However, liberty is granted to the petitioner to file a fresh petition before the Sessions Court after the evidence of the victim is recorded.
